summary.short: Utah SB 132 (2025) creates Utah Code chapter 54-26 on electric service to large load customers. Qualified electric utilities must process service requests; large load contracts require Public Service Commission approval; large-scale generation providers may serve large loads; large loads bear incremental costs. Effective May 7, 2025.
summary.long: The Act enacts Utah Code Chapter 54-26 on large-scale electric service. Large-scale service requests cover new or added service of 100 megawatts or more within five years. Utilities must acknowledge requests, complete evaluations within set deadlines, issue written service proposals, and may charge fees. Large load service must be provided under contracts approved by the Public Service Commission, which approves a contract if the customer bears incremental costs and existing ratepayers do not. Qualified electric utilities have the sole right to serve large loads, except that customers may take alternative service from registered large-scale generation providers if a utility misses deadlines or no agreement is reached within 90 days. Closed private generation and connected generation systems are established, with some exemptions from public utility regulation. Chapter service is exempt from specified rate regulation, and large load costs are excluded from rates. The commission must investigate a large load flexible tariff, set transmission cost-allocation rules for contracts executed on or after January 1, 2026, and review the chapter before October 31, 2027 and every three years. The chapter applies to contracts with service commencing on or before December 31, 2034. The bill takes effect May 7, 2025.

notes: The registry title refers to Rocky Mountain Power and to Electrical Power Amendments; the enrolled text is titled Electric Utility Amendments and does not name that utility. 'Qualified electric utility' is defined generically as a large-scale electric utility (54-26-101(14)). Internal inconsistency: 54-26-102(1)(b) refers to a 'private generation service request', a term that is not defined, while 54-26-201(1) and 54-26-102(1)(d) use 'private generation contract'. The section 54-26-901(5) fee is collected from customers who submit requests. Effective date is May 7, 2025 (Section 22). Relations to federal law are generic references, and no federal instrument is named.
